thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PAGER - metrics-ingest - prometheus-scrape-fanout failures (svc:metrics-pipeline)

pagerduty-bot: Incident: PAGERDUTY-INC-4219 assigned to eng-sre on-call (sophie). Severity: P2.

sophie: acked in PD. I'm on it. Anyone seeing customer impact yet?

maria: noticed dashboards for customer-facing latency are stale since ~08:12 UTC, grafana panels show 'no data' on a few endpoints.

kevin: checking Prom scrapers — saw a spike of 503s from scrape-proxy pool a few mins ago.

raj: seeing increased consumer lag for metrics-topic in Kafka: partition 12 lag ~180k, others ~50-100k. Suspect upstream scrape fanout failing and backlog building.

jin: grep from scrape-proxy logs: ```2026-03-14T08:11:58Z ERROR fanout_manager.go:124 failed fanout to kafka: dial tcp 10.2.0.15:9092: connection refused```

maria: also getting repeated 502s from /internal/metrics-upload endpoint in app logs.

sophie: good. confirm scope: scrapes failing -> fanout to kafka failing -> consumers backlog -> dashboards stale. Customer impact: metrics-driven alerts delayed; some downstream batch jobs depend on these metrics. No direct user-facing API impact yet.

kevin: running quick health checks: `kubectl -n metrics get pods -l app=scrape-proxy` -> pods are Running but `kubectl logs` shows connection resets for kube-ip vs kafka service.

raj: kafka brokers show tcp connections spike. Might be ephemeral port exhaustion on the brokers or network ACL enforcement. Running `kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group metrics-consumers` now.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy: if not acked by senior in 10m, escalate to @oncall-roster.

sophie: I'm escalating to infra to check kafka networking. @jin can you run a quick `ss -tnp` on broker-3 and check TIME_WAIT counts?

jin: on broker-3: TIME_WAIT ~ 92k, many connections in CLOSE_WAIT. Running `netstat -s` shows tcp_tw_reuse disabled. Suspect broker ephemeral port exhaustion.

maria: while infra looks at brokers, can we failover consumers to backup kafka cluster? We have a readonly mirror cluster (kafka-readonly-2) that accepts limited writes — config allows temporary replication.

kevin: that could work for scrapes -> fanout path. Steps: 1) update scrape-proxy config to point to kafka-readonly-2 bootstrap list, 2) restart scrape-proxy pods in rolling fashion, 3) monitor consumer lag and dashboards.

sophie: let's do it. Runbook check: runbook section "metrics kafka failover" v2.1. Oncall will patch configmap and rollout, infra will watch brokers.

raj: I'm prepping the configmap patch now. Patch: ```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: scrape-proxy-config
data:
  KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP: "kafka-readonly-2:9092,kafka-readonly-2:9093"
EOF
```

jin: infra: I'm draining connections on broker-3 and toggling tcp_tw_reuse=1 to reduce TIME_WAIT. Doing sysctl now: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1`

pagerduty-bot: Note: manual change to kernel params recorded in incident timeline. Remember to revert if needed.

maria: applying configmap patch in 30s, will then rollout restart scrape-proxy with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/scrape-proxy -n metrics --timeout=5m`.

sophie: option: limit concurrency on scrapers to avoid re-flooding broker. Change SCRAPE_PARALLELISM from 50 -> 10 during failover. Do that in same configmap.

kevin: +1. Patch will include both KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP and SCRAPE_PARALLELISM=10.

raj: patch applied. Starting rollout.

maria: restart underway. Pod 1/3 terminated, new pod initializing. Logs show `connected to kafka-readonly-2:9092` on new pod.

jin: infra: after tcp_tw_reuse toggle, TIME_WAIT dropped to ~4k on broker-3. Connections stabilizing. Broker CPU still high but acceptable.

sophie: monitoring dashboards: grafana panels starting to populate again. Consumer lag for partition 12 down from 180k -> 4.5k and declining.

kevin: shipping quick alert to customer ops: "We experienced a metrics ingestion outage impacting dashboards and alert freshness between 08:11-08:45 UTC. We have failed over scrape fanout to backup cluster and backlog is processing. We'll follow up with RCA."

pagerduty-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation=failover to kafka-readonly-2; kernel-tweak=tcp_tw_reuse enabled; config-change=scrape parallelism reduced.

sophie: good work. Next: 1) keep an eye on consumer lag until <500 per partition, 2) schedule postmortem and assign to raj+jin, 3) revert kernel tweak only after brokers are stable and we plan persistent config change.

maria: will open a ticket for follow-up with timeline and customer notif text.

kevin: thanks team. I'll hand off to on-call bridge for monitoring for next 2 hours. @oncall-roster you have the handoff.

oncall-roster: Handoff accepted. Monitoring playbook in place. Closing PD incident.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: PAGERDUTY-INC-4219 — mitigated (failover) at 1905004534.

sophie: closing thread, will convert to postmortem template once we have logs and timelines. :white_check_mark:
